Harness 12% Returns: Cullman County, Alabama Tax Lien Investing

Ready for an investment opportunity with up to 12% returns and a chance to acquire valuable property? Cullman County, Alabama, opens the door for you with its Tax Lien Sale every May!

Investing in tax liens can offer high returns compared to traditional investments, with low entry costs for property acquisition. Cullman County’s annual tax lien auction provides an excellent opportunity for savvy investors to capitalize on these benefits.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

A tax lien certificate is a claim against a property for unpaid property taxes. When you purchase a tax lien certificate, you pay the outstanding taxes, and in return, you earn interest on your investment until the property owner pays you back. If the owner fails to redeem the property within a specified period (three years in Cullman County), you may have the opportunity to foreclose on the property.

Steps to Start Tax Lien Investing in Cullman County

1. Research and Understand Local Laws

It’s crucial to understand the legal framework governing tax lien sales in Cullman County. Familiarize yourself with the regulations outlined in Title 40, Chapter 10, Code of Alabama 1975.

2. Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website

Get all necessary information about the tax lien sale from the Cullman County Revenue Commissioner’s website. Key links include:

  • Cullman County Tax Lien Information
  • Cullman County Land Tax Sale Information

3. Check the Auction Site

The tax lien auction is held in person at the County Commission conference room of the Cullman County Courthouse.

4. Read the Details about Tax Liens

Understand the sale schedule, parcel inquiry, and other essential details. The list of delinquent properties is available online up to the auction date.

5. Contact the County Office

If you have any questions, you can contact the revenue office at revenue@co.cullman.al.us.

Pro Tips

  • Do Your Homework: Research properties thoroughly before the auction.
  • Pre-register: Send your registration details to the Revenue Commissioner’s office ahead of time.
  • Bring the Right Payment: Accepted forms include cash, cashier’s check, money order, or credit card.

Important Considerations

  1. Due Diligence: It’s crucial to research properties before bidding. The list of delinquent properties is available online leading up to the auction.
  2. Payment Methods: Ensure you have the appropriate payment form—cash, cashier’s check, or money order—on the auction day.
  3. Legal Process for Ownership: If a property isn’t redeemed within three years, obtaining ownership requires a legal process known as “quieting the title” through the Circuit Court.

FAQs

Q: What happens if the property owner redeems the property?

A: You will receive the amount you paid plus interest at the rate of your winning bid.

Q: How can I participate in the auction?

A: You must pre-register by emailing your details to the revenue office. The auction is held in person at the Cullman County Courthouse.

Q: What payment methods are accepted?

A: You can pay with cash, cashier’s check, money order, or credit card. They do not accept personal checks.
